title: The Cloud of Unknowing
author: Anonymous (Underhill ed)
description: The Cloud of Unknowing, the anonymous fourteenth-century English mystical treatise, edited from the British Museum manuscript with an introduction by Evelyn Underhill (1912). Written by an unknown contemplative priest, probably in the East Midlands, for a young disciple called to the solitary life, it teaches a method of contemplative prayer rooted in the apophatic tradition of Pseudo-Dionysius. God cannot be grasped by the intellect but may be reached by love: the contemplative places all created things, thoughts and even holy images beneath a 'cloud of forgetting' and directs a 'naked intent' of love, often focused in a single short word such as 'God' or 'love', into the 'cloud of unknowing' between the soul and God. Across seventy-five short chapters it gives practical advice on distractions, humility, discretion and signs of a true calling. A classic of English spirituality, it inspired modern centering prayer.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection. Source text obtained from the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/bookofcontemplat00unde).
